title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes Grothendieck is axiomatizing a combinatorial notion of 'figure' (a geometric configuration built from elementary pieces). On p.110 he defined a 'magasin' (store) (M, ≤, ≪, |o|). Here ≤ and ≪ are two partial orders with ≤ ⊂ ≪. |o| is a symmetric, irreflexive binary relation, inherited along the 'minimal ≪' relation. Mag4 says that distinct elements below a common element are |o|-related. Figures of a magasin are ≤-down-closed subsets whose members are pairwise compatible (X ⊼ Y: the non-shared parts are pairwise |o|).

This page introduces the 'global' version, an 'atelier' (workshop, '(specimen)'): (𝓕, ≤, ≪; |o|).
- At1: 𝓕 is nonempty and has the ≤-sup of every bounded-above subfamily. So it is a bounded-complete poset; sup ∅ gives a least element, the empty figure.
- At2: every figure F is the ≤-sup of its 'structures' F̃ = {X ∈ 𝓕 : X ≤ F, X strictly irreducible}. So the completely join-irreducible elements are join-dense.
- Let M = the set of elementary figures (strictly irreducible elements) with the induced ≤. Grothendieck asserts that a poset (𝓕, ≤) satisfying At1–At2 is equivalent to the following data: the poset (M, ≤) together with a family 𝓕̃ of ≤-closed (down-closed) subsets of M (the sets F̃). This family contains each principal down-set, is closed under taking closed subsets (AtM2 on p.112), covers M, and contains ∅. The margin notes that F ≤ G iff F̃ ⊂ G̃.
- The second order ≪ is then to be read off from M: At4 (p.112) says F ≪ G iff every X ∈ F̃ is ≪ some Y ∈ G̃. This is a lower (Hoare-type) powerdomain extension of ≪ from M to 𝓕.
- At3, after several rewrites: if F ≪ G (in this elementwise sense), then F ∨ G exists in 𝓕. He remarks that by At3 it suffices to check things on M.
- On p.112, At3(a) makes the existence of binary joins equivalent to a binary condition: F ∨ G exists iff every X ∈ F̃∖G̃ is |o| every Y ∈ G̃∖F̃. At3(b) says |o| really lives on M.

In modern terms: an atelier is a bounded-complete, join-irreducible-generated poset presented by its 'atoms of structure' M with a binary compatibility relation |o|. Consistency (existence of joins) is then pairwise. The figures are exactly the down-closed, pairwise-compatible subsets of M. This is the shape of the representation of prime-algebraic coherent domains by prime event structures with binary conflict, or of coherence spaces (cliques of a coherence relation), here with an additional 'geometric containment' order ≪ lifted to figures.
errors: The claimed equivalence between posets satisfying At1–At2 and (M, family of closed subsets closed under closed subsets) is false in general if 'strictly irreducible' means only completely join-irreducible. Counterexample: the diamond lattice M3 with atoms a, b, c. Its top is a∨b, so its structure set is {a,b,c}, yet {a,b} is a closed subset of it that is not of the form F̃. The equivalence needs the irreducibles to be completely join-prime (a distributivity / prime-algebraic hypothesis), or else needs F̃ = F̃₁ ∪ F̃₂ for joins. The page does not state this; it may be intended to follow from the |o| axioms (At3a on p.112), but that is not shown.

At3 is left in a garbled state with several crossed-out versions. It is not clear whether F ≪ G should imply only that {F,G} is bounded or that F ∨ G exists; the 'il suffit de le vérifier dans M' reduction is asserted without argument.

ideas.what: Atelier: bounded-complete poset in which every element is the sup of the strictly irreducible elements below it ('structures')
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff (representation of distributive lattices); Scott (domains, 1970s); Nielsen–Plotkin–Winskel 1981 (prime algebraic domains)

ideas.what: Presentation of the atelier by (M, ≤) with a family of down-closed subsets closed under closed subsets, containing principal ideals and ∅, covering M
ideas.modern_name: configurations of a prime event structure / simplicial-complex-like consistency family on a poset (cf. Scott information systems)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nielsen, Plotkin, Winskel (1981); Winskel (1980s); Scott (1982, information systems)

ideas.what: Existence of joins characterized by a binary symmetric irreflexive relation |o| between non-shared elementary pieces (pairwise consistency)
ideas.modern_name: coherence relation / binary conflict-freeness (coherence spaces, event structures with binary conflict, dI-domains)

ideas.what: Lifting a second order ≪ from elementary figures to figures by F ≪ G iff ∀X∈F̃ ∃Y∈G̃ X≪Y
ideas.modern_name: Hoare / lower powerdomain preorder (Egli–Milner lower half)

missed.claim: In a geometric context (analysis situs, figures built from elementary figures), Grothendieck independently arrives at the same combinatorial structure as computer-science domain theory: elementary pieces M, a partial order, a binary compatibility relation determining which sets of pieces form a figure, and figures as down-closed pairwise-compatible sets. This is the structure of prime event structures, coherence spaces and dI-domains, here enriched with a second 'containment' order ≪. No link between his late analysis situs program and event structures / coherence spaces seems to be recorded.
missed.quote: Toute figure est le Sup^≤ des éléments F̃ de ses "structures" F̃ = {X ∈ 𝓕 | X ≤ F, X "strictement irréductible"}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests his 1986 combinatorial foundations of 'figures' could be read, and possibly completed, using event-structure / domain-theoretic representation theorems. Conversely, the extra order ≪ ('geometric containment') is a two-order enrichment not standard in event structures, which might be of interest for concurrency-geometry interfaces (e.g. directed topology).

missed.claim: The axiomatics of 'ateliers' vs 'magasins' (the equivalence between global posets of figures and local data on elementary figures) is left incomplete. The representation theorem as stated needs a primeness/distributivity hypothesis that is not supplied.
missed.quote: Par At 3, il suffit de le vérifier dans M.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor: a precise statement would be a routine exercise in lattice/domain theory, but would clarify what class of geometric 'figures' he intended.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics itself is elementary order theory. It is mildly notable that in 1986, for geometric purposes, Grothendieck independently sets up a structure matching prime event structures / coherence spaces (pairwise coherence plus down-closure), with a lifted powerdomain-type order. That connection does not appear to be noted anywhere, but it is not deep.
transcription_corrections: In the header the third datum is the relation |o| (as on p.110 and p.112), not '|·|'.
At1 reads: '𝓕 ≠ ∅ et 𝓕 stable par Sup^≤ de [familles] majorées quelconques', i.e. sups of arbitrary bounded-above families.
The struck-out At3 line reads 'X ∪ Y existe dans 𝓕 (i.e. {X, Y} majoré pour ≤)'; the active version is 'F ≪ G ... alors F ∪ G existe dans 𝓕'.
Left margin begins: 'F ≤ G équivalent à F̃ ⊂ G̃ (condition sur structures) ...'.
